anomalies.observed: The ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch is implemented with T3 marked 'AO3400A' (a 30 V N-MOSFET), with its drain on the 24 V solenoid node (flyback D3 SS34 to +24V) and gate driven via R3 100R from NET0003 through T7 BT3904.
anomalies.expected: Specification §2 states the ATO valve switch is 'T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET)', a 60 V device. Switching a 24 V inductive solenoid load with a 30 V-rated FET leaves almost no margin for transients; a 60 V part is required.

evidence.quote: Sheet 1, 'ATO Valve' block (page 3 tile): 'T3 AO3400A' with drain to the 24 V valve node (H13 MC_0.2", D3 SS34, C43/C21)

anomalies.impact: The valve-driving MOSFET is rated 30 V instead of the specified 60 V; turn-off transients on the 24 V solenoid can exceed Vds rating, causing premature failure or avalanche stress of the ATO valve switch.

anomalies.observed: In the 'Water Height Sensor' block, the LiDAR PR5 is wired through header H4 to the main I2C bus (NET0084/NET0017) and +5V/GND.
anomalies.expected: Specification §4.3/§6: the TF-Luna LiDAR 'pins are typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design' and it is marked on_board: no; the intended design leaves it unwired.

anomalies.impact: A 5 V-powered LiDAR module is connected to the 3.3 V I2C bus; if a module with 5 V pull-ups/levels is plugged in, bus high levels are driven above the ESP32-C6's 3.3 V domain, and the board's behavior deviates from the documented (unwired) design.

The first finding is the most consequential; the rest of the power train, isolators, TMC2209 drivers and pump switches match the specification's topology.
